title: Cocoa Bean Production
prompt: The table below shows cocoa bean production in six regions between 1992 and 1998. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table indicates cocoa bean production in tons from six different regions worldwide during the period from 1992 to 1998.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while most regions experienced fluctuations in their output over the years, South America showed a consistent downward trend. Additionally, Africa was by far the largest producer of cocoa beans throughout the given timeframe, with its production significantly exceeding all other regions combined.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding high-producing regions, Africa dominated with 1,397,000 tons in 1992, triple South America's 568,000 tons and Asia's 416,000 tons. Thereafter, Africa's output peaked at 1,920,000 tons in 1996 before settling at 1,822,000 tons in 1998, showing 30% overall growth. South America, however, declined steadily to 333,000 tons by 1998, a 40% decrease. Meanwhile, Asia's production peaked at 498,000 tons in 1994 before stabilizing around 415,000 tons.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining regions, The Caribbean and North Central America had similar 1992 outputs, at 52,000 and 50,000 tons respectively, while Oceania ranked lowest at 42,000 tons. By 1998, Caribbean production had increased to 68,000 tons, North Central America returned to its initial 50,000 tons after a temporary decline, and Oceania fell to 34,000 tons, a 20% decrease from its starting figure.
